hooks.prompt:
You are checking whether a user's message contains a tangential idea worth capturing to their Obsidian vault.

Hook input JSON:
$ARGUMENTS

An idea is a future project concept, a "what if" thought, or a side tangent that is NOT a direct task instruction. Signals include: "I had an idea about...", "What if we..." / "What if I...", "It would be cool to..." / "It would be nice if...", "We should eventually..." / "Someday we should...", "Note to self..." / "Remind me to think about...", "That gives me an idea...", "A tangent but..." / "Side thought...", "For the future..." / "Down the road...", "I want to eventually...", or any sentence describing something to build, explore, or investigate that is not the current task.

Do NOT treat these as ideas: direct task instructions ("fix this bug", "add this feature"), questions ("how does X work?"), complaints or frustrations, or ideas the user is actively implementing right now.

If the message contains an idea, respond with exactly this JSON:
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"The user mentioned a tangential idea. Call obsidian_float_idea with the idea text. Do NOT ask which project, let auto-routing handle it, or pass the project if it is obvious from context. Then confirm in one short line ('Captured to {project}.') and continue with what they actually asked. If the idea describes a project that does not exist yet (new product, new repo, new initiative), call obsidian_incubate_project instead with a name and description."}}

Otherwise respond with exactly this JSON:
{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit"}}

Return only the JSON object and nothing else.
